property-development-is-an-information-p.heading: Fieldwork: the ten-minute evidence audit
body: Before spending another pound on an opportunity, open the project and list the five facts currently carrying the decision. A typical list might include ownership of the required land, existing lawful use, likely planning principle, achievable development value and an assumed construction rate. For each fact, write the source and date. If the source is a seller statement, marketing brochure, old valuation, screenshot or memory, classify it accordingly. Then ask which unsupported proposition could change the decision most. That becomes the next evidence task. This exercise takes minutes and prevents a sophisticated project from resting on one undocumented assumption.

Repeat the audit whenever the scheme changes materially. A larger unit count may change parking, BNG, affordable housing, CIL, access or fire strategy. A revised red line may create a title question. A new structural solution may alter cost and programme. The evidence ledger should therefore move with the proposal. Development intelligence is not a report produced once at acquisition; it is a maintained relationship between the current scheme and the evidence that supports it.

planning-intelligence-after-nppf-2026.heading: Fieldwork: run a current-policy challenge before design freeze
body: Before design freeze, ask the planning workflow to produce a one-page challenge note containing the current national baseline, adopted local policies most likely to decide the proposal, any material emerging policy, relevant supplementary guidance, validation triggers, nearby refusals and appeal reasoning. Then ask the architect and planning adviser to identify which design decisions answer those issues. This forces the team to connect policy to the scheme while changes are still affordable.

The note should also list what has not been established. If the authority's current parking standard cannot be found, say so. If affordable-housing thresholds depend on a policy interpretation, identify the question. If an appeal appears supportive but the site context is materially different, record the distinction. The objective is not to create a document that proves the scheme is acceptable. It is to expose the planning questions that deserve conscious design or evidence before the application is fixed.

planning-applications-that-are-easier-to.heading: Fieldwork: perform a refusal rehearsal
body: One week before submission, run a refusal rehearsal. Write the strongest plausible refusal reason for each material topic: principle, design, amenity, highways, parking, heritage, ecology, drainage, noise, trees or any site-specific issue. Then identify the exact drawing, report, policy argument or factual evidence that would answer it. If the response is merely 'the officer should agree', the application may not yet be evidentially ready.

This rehearsal is not about manufacturing certainty or writing the authority's decision in advance. It is a quality-control exercise. It frequently reveals small but important disconnects — a planning statement referencing an old drawing, a transport note using a superseded unit count, a privacy argument without a dimension, or a consultant conclusion whose assumptions no longer match the design. Correcting those issues before submission is usually cheaper than explaining them after validation or consultation.

development-appraisal-and-residual-land-.heading: Fieldwork: annotate the appraisal with evidence grades
body: Take the current appraisal and place one evidence grade beside every material input. 'A' might mean a current evidenced figure such as a signed quotation or verified statutory fee; 'B' might mean a reasonable current benchmark requiring later refinement; 'C' might mean an early assumption; and 'U' might mean unknown. The labels are less important than the discipline. Once the sheet is annotated, sort attention by both financial sensitivity and evidence weakness.

A £5,000 uncertain line may not deserve the same investigation as a £200,000 GDV assumption, but a seemingly small statutory or technical issue can still block the scheme entirely. The commercial review should therefore consider both monetary impact and decision impact. Where a policy obligation is known to be relevant but the amount is unknown, keep it visibly unresolved. A model that contains blanks with named verification actions can be more decision-useful than one in which every cell has been populated by a guess.

title-maps-and-unregistered-land.heading: Fieldwork: create the land-control schedule
body: For any site where access, boundary or third-party land could affect development, create a simple land-control schedule. List every title or land interest identified, the registered proprietor where evidenced, tenure, rights benefiting the site, rights burdening it, covenants or restrictions that appear material, areas where mapping is uncertain and any land that the proposed red line uses but the evidence has not yet tied to the applicant's control. Link each row to the actual title or search evidence.

Then give the schedule to the conveyancer with development questions rather than a generic request to review title. Ask whether the proposed access is supported by the rights, whether any covenant affects the intended use or works, whether a lease requires consent, whether a gap needs a Search of the Index Map and whether the planning red line is consistent with the land-control position. This makes legal due diligence directly useful to design and appraisal.

procurement-and-quote-intelligence.heading: Fieldwork: score quote comparability before price
body: Before looking at which contractor is cheapest, score how comparable the quotations actually are. Check scope coverage, drawing revision, specification, quantities, preliminaries, access, waste, protection, temporary works, testing, commissioning, making good, design responsibility, programme, provisional sums and exclusions. A quote that cannot be reconciled to the common scope should remain 'clarification required' even if its headline total is attractive.

After clarification, record the commercial adjustments separately from the bidder's original price. Do not rewrite the contractor's offer as if the clarifications had always been included. The appointment record should show original quotation, clarification, agreed adjustment and final accepted basis. This preserves the audit trail that will later matter when a variation is disputed or an allowance is exhausted. AI can accelerate the comparison, but the commercial baseline must remain evidence-backed.

document-intelligence-and-evidence-room.heading: Fieldwork: perform an evidence-room health check
body: Once a month on an active project, run an evidence-room health check. Identify superseded drawings still referenced by live records, professional conclusions with unverified assumptions, claims that lack a source, approvals without approval evidence, documents whose retention or ownership is unclear and contradictory facts appearing in different files. Prioritise issues that could affect money, programme, compliance, safety, planning or legal rights.

The health check should produce actions rather than a score for its own sake. Replace a superseded reference, ask the consultant to confirm whether a conclusion still applies, obtain the missing instruction, correct the project record or mark the issue as unresolved. This routine is particularly valuable when AI is used heavily because it prevents a well-written synthesis from hiding deterioration in the underlying evidence base.

a-90-day-implementation-plan.heading: Fieldwork: the day-90 operating review
body: On day 90, review the system with actual project evidence rather than a demo dataset. Choose one site that was screened, one professional brief, one commercial comparison and one project-control sequence. For each, compare the old process with the new: time taken, evidence found, decisions clarified, errors prevented, manual rework and any new risks introduced by automation. Ask users which outputs they trust and which they still work around outside the platform.

Then freeze a version-one operating standard. Define the required site fields, approved data sources, project naming, review states, calculator assumptions, authority boundaries, document-handling rules, AI escalation rules and minimum registers. Assign someone to maintain the standard. The final implementation milestone is not 'AI deployed'. It is that the business can explain how a development decision moves from input to evidence, analysis, verification, decision and retained record — and can repeat that process next week without rebuilding it from scratch.
